lesson_title: Why There Are Only Five Fair Dice
hook_text: A die with identical regular faces and identical corners comes in only five shapes: 4, 6, 8, 12 or 20 faces. Never 30. Here is the 2000-year-old reason.
clip_script: A perfectly fair die needs every face the same regular shape and every corner the same. Only five solids manage it. Here is why. Look at one corner. At least three faces meet there, and their angles must add to less than 360 degrees, or the corner goes flat. Triangles have 60 degree corners. Three triangles: 180, the 4-sided die. Four: 240, the 8-sided die. Five: 300, the 20-sided die. Six: 360. Flat. Done. Squares, 90 degrees. Three: 270, the ordinary cube. Four: flat. Pentagons, 108. Three: 324, the 12-sided die. Four: 432, too big. Hexagons, 120. Three: 360, flat like a honeycomb. Anything bigger cannot even fit three. Five solids, proven over two thousand years ago. Every fair die in every board game is one of them.
visual_style: Triangles slide round a glowing point one at a time, folding up into corners and finally lying flat at six; squares, pentagons and hexagons follow; the five solids spin in a row with their side counts.
pacing: Quick hook, a steady count of corners, a beat at each flat case, a confident close.
